newsitem.title: ISRAEL: PLO demands U.S. halt loan guarantees to Israel.
newsitem.headline: PLO demands U.S. halt loan guarantees to Israel.

text.p: Palestinian officials demanded on Friday that the United States freeze its loan guarantees to Israel in response to the Jewish state's settlement policy in the West Bank and Gaza Strip.

"We are undertaking a campaign to confront the settlement policy because this is the main danger which threatens us," said Palestinian Planning Minister Nabil Shaath after the weekly cabinet meeting in Gaza.
"We are demanding the American administration stop its loan guarantees to Israel," Shaath said, adding: "We will move in all directions to confront Israel's settlement policy."

Israel raised Palestinian ire with a decision last week to grant financial benefits to Jewish settlements in the West Bank. The Israeli action followed the killing of a settler mother and her son by Arab gunmen.

A White House spokesman said Washington found the latest policy on settlements "a complicating factor" in peace efforts which have been stuck on the long-overdue handover of 80 percent of the West Bank town of Hebron to Palestinian rule.

Israel's relations with Washington reached a 35-year low in the early 1990s over a settlement boom spearheaded by right-wing Likud Party prime minister Yitzhak Shamir and his hawkish housing minister Ariel Sharon.

Former president George Bush held up $10 billion in U.S. loan guarantees over the settlement issue, awarding them only after Yitzhak Rabin ousted Shamir and Likud in 1993 and froze new settlement building.

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, now the Likud leader, lifted the freeze after winning office last May. About 130,000 Jews live in the settlements scattered among two million Palestinians in the West Bank and Gaza.
U.S. Middle East envoy Dennis Ross will try to alleviate Israeli-Palestinian tensions and clinch a deal on Hebron during a weekend trip to the region, the State Department said on Friday.
State Department spokesman Nicholas Burns said, however, that Ross's brief trip was unlikely to produce an immediate agreement on an Israeli troop pullback in the West Bank town.

Netanyahu has demanded that the original agreement, signed by the former Israeli government, be altered to ensure the safety of 400 Jews who live among more than 100,000 Arabs in Hebron. The Palestinians reject any changes to the accord.
